messages:
jen: quick heads-up — prod lambda started failing KMS decrypt after yesterday's key rotation. CloudWatch shows: 
```
2026-02-11T16:22:01.123Z ERROR decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::999888777666:assumed-role/ci-deploy-role/session123 is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333444:key/abcd-ef01-2345-6789
status code: 400, request id: 3a4b5c
```
jen: lambda assumes a role in account 111222333444 via our CI (999888777666) flow — this used to work before rotation.
matt: can you paste the exact error and which principal the function is actually using (assumed role ARN)?
jen: saw this in CloudTrail userIdentity: type: "AssumedRole", arn: "arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/deploy-runner/ci-session" — so the KMS caller principal is in the target account.
nana: did we create any grants during rotation? grants can get invalidated if the key material or key object changes.
jen: ran `aws kms list-grants --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333444:key/abcd-ef01-2345-6789 --profile prod` -> `[]` (empty)
matt: ok no grants. That implies access should be via key policy + IAM.
jen: here's the key policy the rotation tool applied (redacted):
```
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[
    {"Sid":"RootAccount","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111222333444:root"},"Action":["kms:List*","kms:Describe*"],"Resource":"*"},
    {"Sid":"AllowSourceRole","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::999888777666:role/ci-deploy-role"},"Action":["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],"Resource":"*"}
  ]
}
```
jen: note the template inserted the 999... role ARN (source CI account) instead of the assumed-role in the target account.
nana: that will not match the actual caller principal. For cross-account assume-role flows, KMS sees the assumed-role principal in the account where the call originates (here: arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/deploy-runner/...). Granting the source account role ARN in the key policy doesn't help once there was an sts assume into the target account.
matt: two fixes: 1) edit the key policy to allow the target account root (arn:aws:iam::111222333444:root) kms:Decrypt/kms:GenerateDataKey so normal IAM policies in that account can be used, OR 2) list the assumed-role principal pattern in the key policy (e.g., arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/deploy-runner/*). Prefer 1 for durability.
jen: the deploy-runner role in acct 111222333444 does have an inline policy allowing kms:Decrypt against the key ARN.
jen: role policy snippet:
```
{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],"Resource":["arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333444:key/abcd-ef01-2345-6789"]}
```
matt: then the key policy must authorize the account or the IAM principals; but I see your root account statement only allows List/Describe, not Decrypt. So IAM in the account can't use the key.
nana: yep the rotation automation accidentally narrowed the root/account statement to management-only actions. That removed kms:Decrypt from the account-level allow.
sam: short-term mitigation: create a grant that explicitly permits the assumed role to Decrypt. Grants persist for the key material lifetime but will break on rotation — so only temporary.
jen: created a temp grant: `aws kms create-grant --key-id <id> --grantee-principal arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/deploy-runner/ci-session --operations Decrypt --name temp-deploy-grant` -> returned GrantId 1234-5678. After that lambda succeeded.
matt: good. For long-term, patch the key policy. Example statement to re-add:
```
{"Sid":"AllowAccountUse","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111222333444:root"},"Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],"Resource":"*"}
```
jen: patched the policy at 2026-02-11T17:03:00Z, tested — decrypts OK. Removed the temporary grant.
nana: follow-ups we should do: add a unit test in the rotation tool that validates the produced key policy contains account-level kms:Decrypt/kms:GenerateDataKey, add a post-rotation canary that assumes the target role and runs a decrypt smoke test, and require security sign-off for key policy changes.
matt: also add a short runbook note about cross-account principal semantics for KMS (assumed-role vs source-role ARN) and a snippet for creating one-off grants if needed.
sam: :thumbsup: also remind infra team that grants are ephemeral and tied to specific key material/version; avoid relying on grants across rotations.
jen: thanks everyone, reverted rotation template, added PR with tests. Saved my evening :relieved:
